description: We are students of the first year of Space Engineering at Agh in Kraków
summary: We developed an algorythm, which searches through terrestial data, finding matching analogs for lunar and martian terrain on Earth. It emphasises topographical similarities, by comparing elevation histograms of candidate landing sites and bases on the Moon and Mars with the Earth's elevation data, simultaneously filtering out obvious mismatches (forested areas, bodies of water). This approach enables first-stage locating terrestial sites suitable for development and testing of lunar and martian technologies in resembling terrain. While sites like Death Valley are already well - researched and known, our solution searches for all topographically - suitable locations. Numerous space companies can benefit from our solution during selection of testing locations.
details:
What does it do and how does it actually work?

Our solution first determines the topographical conditions on candidate landing sites on the South Pole of the Moon and potential landing/base locations on Mars. The algorythm compares the histograms of elevation and slope between the obtained data for individual sites on the Moon or Mars and the Earth's data. The results are filtered based on land coverage and surface water occurrence. The found locations are then portrayed on a visual map, which enables immediate assessment of general reliabilty of the results from a satellite image.

What benefits does it offer?

Our approach enables discovering hitherto unknown Earth locations that analog lunar and martian terrain. Companies and agencies from the space sector may benefit from our solution during the first stage of seeking potential test sites and research labs.

How can it be further developed?

Further development could include addition of parameters and customisation of the weights. The tool's applicability may reach other engineering sectors and tourism. Fully customizable search engine based on our solution would be useful in countless Earth-data studies.

What tools did we use?

Data analysis: QGIS, Python
